setup_name: Trailing Stop — ATR Multiple Exit
keywords: trailing stop, ATR, dynamic exit, trend following, protection
description: Exit using a trailing stop set at 2-3x ATR from the current price. In trending markets, this allows the trade to breathe while protecting profits. For longs, trail below the low; for shorts, trail above the high. Tighten by 0.5x ATR when volume drops below 50% of average, signaling the move is exhausting. The ATR multiple adapts to volatility automatically — wider in volatile markets, tighter in calm ones.

setup_name: Chandelier Exit — Highest High Trailing
keywords: chandelier exit, highest high, trailing, trend protection
description: The Chandelier Exit hangs a trailing stop 3x ATR below the highest high (for longs) or above the lowest low (for shorts). Named because it 'hangs from the ceiling' of the price action. Adjust the ATR multiplier: use 2.5x for quick exits, 4x for longer trends. This exit keeps you in strong trends but gets you out when the trend reverses by more than the average range.

setup_name: Percentage Trailing Stop — Fixed Distance
keywords: trailing stop, percentage, fixed, profit protection, simple
description: Trail a stop loss at a fixed percentage below the highest close since entry. For crypto, use 3-5% for scalps, 5-8% for swing trades, 10-15% for position trades. Move the stop up every candle but never move it down (for longs). This is the simplest trailing mechanism but doesn't adapt to volatility. Best used when ATR data isn't available or as a fallback.

setup_name: Volatility-Adjusted Trailing Stop — VIX Regime
keywords: volatility adjusted, VIX, regime, adaptive trailing, dynamic
description: Adjust trailing stop distance based on the current volatility regime. When ATR is in the top 20% of its 50-day range, use 4x ATR trailing (wider stops for volatile moves). When ATR is in the bottom 20%, use 1.5x ATR (tighter stops for calm markets). In the middle range, use 2.5x ATR. This prevents getting stopped out by noise in volatile markets while taking profits quickly in calm markets.

setup_name: Parabolic SAR Trailing Exit
keywords: parabolic SAR, trend following, trailing, reversal detection
description: Use Parabolic SAR (step=0.02, max=0.2) as the trailing stop mechanism. Enter when SAR flips to the opposite side of price. Exit when SAR flips back. In strong trends, SAR accelerates and stays close to price, locking in profits. In choppy markets, SAR whipsaws — combine with ADX>25 filter to avoid false exits. Best for trending crypto markets where momentum persists.

setup_name: Risk-to-Zero Trailing — Breakeven Acceleration
keywords: risk to zero, breakeven, trailing, acceleration, profit protection
description: Move stop to breakeven as soon as price moves 1R in your favor (where R = initial risk). Then trail at 1R intervals: when price reaches 2R, move stop to 1R profit. At 3R, move to 2R profit. This acceleration ensures you never give back more than 1R after breakeven. Entry at 100, stop at 96 (4R = 1R), target at 108 (2R). At 104, stop to 100 (breakeven). At 108, stop to 104.

setup_name: Half Position Trailing — Split Exit Strategy
keywords: half position, split exit, scaled, trailing, conservative aggressive
description: Exit half the position at 1R profit using a fixed target, then trail the remaining half with a wider ATR-based stop (3-4x ATR). This guarantees you bank profit on the first half while letting the second half run in strong trends. If the trade reverses after the first target, you still have profits. If the trend continues, the second half captures large wins.

setup_name: Time-Based Exit — N-Bar Expiration
keywords: time based, N-bar, expiration, maximum hold, time decay
description: Exit the trade if it hasn't reached 1R profit within N bars. For 1h charts, use N=12 (half a day). For 15m charts, use N=16 (4 hours). If price hasn't moved in your favor within a reasonable time, the setup has failed and capital is better deployed elsewhere. Combine with breakeven stop: if trade is flat after N/2 bars, move stop to breakeven.

setup_name: Session Close Exit — End of Day
keywords: session close, end of day, EOD, overnight risk, gap risk
description: Close all positions before the trading session ends to avoid overnight gap risk. For crypto, close before the lowest-volume period (00-04 UTC). This eliminates gap risk entirely but sacrifices overnight moves. Best for scalpers and intraday traders who don't want exposure to news events outside their monitoring hours.

setup_name: Weekend Flat Exit — Clear Before Saturday
keywords: weekend flat, Saturday, gap risk, weekend risk, crypto gap
description: Crypto liquidity drops 40-60% on weekends. Close positions Friday 20:00 UTC if the trade hasn't reached 2R profit. Weekend gaps can be 10-20% in a single Saturday candle. If holding over the weekend, reduce position size by 50% and set stops at 1.5x normal distance. This exit is especially important before major news events (FOMC, ETF decisions).

setup_name: Kill Zone Time Filter — Only Trade Active Hours
keywords: kill zone, session, London, New York, optimal hours, time filter
description: Only enter trades during kill zones: London 07:00-09:00 UTC and New York 13:00-16:00 UTC. These windows have 65%+ of daily volume. Trades entered outside kill zones have 30% lower win rate. If a trade is still open outside kill zones, tighten stops to breakeven or 0.5x ATR.

setup_name: Maximum Duration Exit — 48-Hour Cap
keywords: maximum duration, time cap, 48 hours, stale trade, opportunity cost
description: Hard cap: exit any trade that hasn't reached 2R within 48 hours on 1h timeframe. Stale trades tie up margin and attention. After 48 hours, either the thesis was wrong or the market is consolidating — either way, capital is better deployed elsewhere. If the trade is in profit but below 2R, consider moving to breakeven and giving it 12 more hours.

setup_name: Opposing Liquidity Pool Target — Where Smart Money Exits
keywords: liquidity pool, opposing, smart money, target, take profit
description: Set profit targets at opposing liquidity pools (major support/resistance levels where pending orders cluster). For longs, target the next resistance where sell orders accumulate. For shorts, target support where buy orders sit. These levels are where institutional players take profits and initiate reversals. Use volume profile to identify High Volume Nodes (HVN) as natural targets.

setup_name: Round Number Target — Psychological Level Exit
keywords: round number, psychological level, 000, 500, target, magnet
description: Crypto price is magnetized to round numbers: BTC at 100K, 105K, 110K. These levels see massive order clustering and profit-taking. Set targets just below round numbers for longs (at 99,800 instead of 100,000). Exit 50% at the first round number, trail the rest. This captures predictable profit-taking behavior.

setup_name: Fibonacci Extension Target — 1.272 and 1.618
keywords: fibonacci, extension, 1.272, 1.618, golden ratio, target
description: Use Fibonacci extensions of the impulse wave to set targets. The 1.272 extension is the minimum profit target. The 1.618 (golden ratio) is the primary target. Scale out: take 1/3 at 1.272, 1/3 at 1.618, trail the last 1/3. This gives defined targets without guessing.

setup_name: Risk-Reward Target — Fixed R-Multiple Exit
keywords: risk reward, R-multiple, 2R, 3R, fixed target, systematic
description: Set profit targets at fixed R-multiples: 2R minimum, 3R target. If risk is 2% ($200 on $10K), then 2R = 4% ($400) and 3R = 6% ($600). This ensures a minimum 2:1 reward-to-risk ratio on every trade. Use breakeven stop after 1R. Take 50% at 2R, trail the rest for potential 3R+.

setup_name: Beacon Target System — 30/50/70% Bollinger Levels
keywords: beacon, bollinger, mean reversion, 30%, 50%, 70%, target system
description: When entering mean reversion trades, use the Bollinger %b as the target system. Enter when %b < 0.30 (oversold). Target 1: %b returns to 0.50 (middle band) — take 50% off. Target 2: %b reaches 0.70 — take another 30%. Trail the remaining 20%. If %b goes above 0.85, exit everything as this signals a breakout rather than reversion.

setup_name: Auction Cap — Too Expensive Rejection Exit
keywords: auction cap, too expensive, rejection, scale out, resistance
description: When price reaches an auction cap (a level where buyers are no longer willing to pay higher prices), aggressive selling appears. Scale out 50% at the first rejection. If price breaks through on the second attempt, the cap has broken — go full size. If it holds, exit the remaining position at breakeven.

setup_name: RSI Divergence Exit — Momentum Exhaustion
keywords: RSI, divergence, momentum, exhaustion, reversal signal
description: Exit when RSI diverges from price. For longs: price makes higher high but RSI makes lower high (bearish divergence). For shorts: price makes lower low but RSI makes higher low (bullish divergence). Exit immediately on divergence confirmation (2 candles). This is the most reliable exit signal across all market conditions — it captures momentum exhaustion before the price reverses.

setup_name: MACD Cross Exit — Trend Reversal
keywords: MACD, cross, signal line, trend reversal, exit
description: Exit longs when MACD line crosses below signal line. Exit shorts when MACD crosses above signal. Use standard 12/26/9 settings. The MACD histogram declining for 3+ consecutive bars before the cross gives early warning. Combine with price action: MACD cross + break of 21 EMA = strong exit signal.

setup_name: Volume Exhaustion Exit — Selling/Buying Climax
keywords: volume, exhaustion, climax, selling, buyers, reversal
description: When volume spikes to 5x average (selling/buying climax), it signals panic and imminent reversal. For profitable longs, volume exhaustion on the upside (5x volume at the top) signals the last of the buyers are entering — exit. Monitor volume ratio: when it exceeds 4x average, start tightening stops. At 5x+, exit 50%. At 6x+, exit everything.

setup_name: Bollinger Band Width Expansion Exit — Move Complete
keywords: bollinger, band width, expansion, squeeze, move complete
description: When Bollinger Band width expands to more than 2.5x its 20-period moving average after a squeeze, the explosive move is likely complete. Enter on squeeze, exit on expansion completion. Exit 75% of the position when width crosses 2.5x average. Trail the remaining 25% with a tight stop.

setup_name: EMA Crossover Exit — Trend Death Signal
keywords: EMA crossover, trend death, moving average, exit signal
description: Exit longs when the fast EMA (9) crosses below the medium EMA (21). Exit shorts when fast crosses above medium. For more confirmation, wait for the medium EMA to cross the 200 EMA — this confirms a secular trend change. The EMA crossover exit has a 1-3 bar lag but produces very few false signals in trending markets.

setup_name: Candlestick Reversal Pattern Exit — Pin Bar/Doji
keywords: candlestick, pin bar, doji, reversal, pattern, exit
description: Exit when a reversal candlestick pattern appears at a key level. For longs: pin bar (long upper wick) at resistance = exit. Doji after strong candles = indecision = exit 50%. Engulfing pattern opposite direction = exit. Require the pattern at a level (support, resistance, EMA, VWAP). Random reversal patterns without level confluence have 50%+ failure rates.

setup_name: VWAP Reversion Exit — Price Returns to Value
keywords: VWAP, reversion, mean reversion, price to value, exit
description: When price deviates more than 2 standard deviations from VWAP, exit as price will revert. Exit longs when price is above VWAP + 2SD and starts declining. Exit shorts when price is below VWAP - 2SD and starts rising. This captures the mean reversion profit at the optimal moment in ranging markets.

setup_name: Higher Low Failure Exit — Trend Structure Break
keywords: higher low, trend structure, break, failure, exit
description: For long positions in an uptrend, exit when price breaks below the previous higher low. This means market structure has shifted to lower highs/lower lows. For shorts, exit when price breaks above the previous lower high. A break of the most recent higher low is an immediate exit — no second chances.

setup_name: Absorption Pattern Exit — Hidden Sellers/Buyers
keywords: absorption, hidden sellers, buyers, order book, exit
description: Absorption pattern: massive volume at a level but price doesn't move. This means large limit orders are absorbing all market orders. For longs, when 5x+ volume at resistance and price doesn't break through, exit 75% — smart money is unloading into the buying pressure.

setup_name: Open Drive Failure Exit — Trend Bar Reversal
keywords: open drive, trend bar, failure, reversal, first hour
description: An open drive is a strong trend bar in the first hour. If this bar is completely reversed within 2 bars, the trend has failed — exit immediately. This signals that institutional flow has reversed. Don't wait for confirmation — the move is over.

setup_name: Breakeven Stop — Risk-Free After 1R
keywords: breakeven, stop loss, risk free, 1R, protection
description: Move stop loss to entry price when price reaches 1R in profit. This makes the trade risk-free. Use this as minimum protection for all trades. Some traders use 'breakeven +0.1%' to cover fees, making the trade truly cost-neutral. The psychological benefit is enormous: once at breakeven, you can let the trade develop without fear.

setup_name: Daily Max Loss Exit — Circuit Breaker
keywords: daily max loss, circuit breaker, 2% rule, risk management
description: If total trades today result in a net loss exceeding 2% of account, stop trading for the day. This is a hard circuit breaker. No exceptions. Track cumulative P&L throughout the session. When you hit -2%, close all positions. This single rule has saved more accounts than any strategy.

setup_name: Weekly Loss Limit — Drawdown Protection
keywords: weekly loss, drawdown, protection, 6% rule, risk management
description: If cumulative losses exceed 6% of account in a week, reduce position sizes by 50% for the next week. If losses exceed 10%, stop trading entirely for the rest of the week. Use weekly P&L tracking. This prevents catastrophic drawdowns while giving room for normal variance.

setup_name: Correlation Risk Exit — Multiple Positions Same Direction
keywords: correlation, risk, multiple positions, same direction, portfolio
description: If you have 3+ positions in the same direction and they're correlated (>0.7), exit the weakest one. Correlated positions compound risk. Reduce to maximum 2 correlated positions. BTC and ETH are correlated; BTC long + SOL short = uncorrelated = OK.

setup_name: News Event Exit — Pre-Announcement Close
keywords: news event, announcement, FOMC, ETF, CPI, pre-announcement, exit
description: Close 50% of all positions 30 minutes before scheduled high-impact events (FOMC, CPI, ETF decisions). The remaining 50% stays with stops moved to breakeven. Never hold full size through binary events. Post-announcement, reassess and re-enter on the new trend.

setup_name: Scale Out 1/3 — Three-Tier Profit Taking
keywords: scale out, 1/3, three-tier, profit taking, systematic
description: 1st third at 1R (guarantee a win). 2nd third at 2R (solid profit). 3rd third trails with 3x ATR stop (runner for big wins). Even if the runner is stopped at breakeven, you've locked in 1R average. If the runner wins, average becomes 2.3R. Over a series, this beats any single-target exit.

setup_name: Scale Out 50-30-20 — Conservative-Aggressive Split
keywords: scale out, 50-30-20, conservative, aggressive, profit taking
description: Take 50% off at 1R (conservative). Take 30% off at 2R (solid). Let 20% run with trailing stop at 3x ATR (aggressive). The 50% at 1R ensures the trade pays for itself. The 20% runner is free money. Over 100 trades, this yields consistent 1.4R average profit.

setup_name: All-or-Nothing Exit — Full Position at Target
keywords: all or nothing, full position, target, binary exit, simple
description: Set a single target at 2R and exit the entire position there. No scaling, no trailing. Simple and mechanical. Best for ranging markets where moves are predictable and limited. The advantage: zero emotional decisions. Best for scalpers and traders who struggle with scaling decisions.

setup_name: Re-Entry After Stop — Failed Breakout Reversal
keywords: re-entry, failed breakout, reversal, second chance, stop loss
description: When stopped out, don't re-enter in the same direction unless: (1) price retests the level, (2) volume is 2x+ the failed breakout volume, (3) the reversal candle closes strong. Wait for the next kill zone session at minimum. Failed breakouts often produce the strongest reversals, but the setup must be clean.

setup_name: Gap Fill Exit — Overnight Gap Target
keywords: gap fill, overnight, weekend gap, target, reversion
description: When a crypto gaps overnight or over the weekend, trade the fill. 70%+ of crypto gaps fill within 24 hours. For gap-up entries, target the fill back to the previous close. Exit 50% at the gap fill, trail the rest. If the gap doesn't fill within 12 hours, exit at breakeven.

setup_name: Open Range Breakdown — First Hour Range Exit
keywords: open range, first hour, range, breakdown, breakout
description: Define the first hour's range. If price breaks out and then reverses back inside within 2 bars, it's a failed breakout — exit immediately and enter the other direction. Failed breakouts from the first hour range have 65%+ reversal probability. Target the opposite side of the range.

setup_name: Momentum Exhaustion — Consecutive Same-Color Candles
keywords: momentum, exhaustion, consecutive candles, reversal, exit
description: After 7+ consecutive same-color candles on 1h, momentum is exhausted. Exit 75% of the position. After 9+ consecutive, exit everything. This pattern has 70%+ reversal probability. Combined with RSI>80 or <20, this is one of the most reliable exhaustion exits in crypto.

setup_name: Regime Change Exit — Trend to Range Transition
keywords: regime change, trend to range, transition, ADX, exit
description: When ADX drops below 20 after being above 30, the market is transitioning from trending to ranging. Exit trending strategies and switch to mean-reversion parameters. Tighten stops to breakeven and reduce position sizes by 50%. The regime change is the most important exit signal because it invalidates your entire thesis.

setup_name: Spread Cost Exit — Illiquid Market Warning
keywords: spread, illiquid, slippage, cost, warning, market quality
description: When bid-ask spread widens to more than 2x normal, exit immediately. Wide spreads indicate liquidity withdrawal — market makers are stepping away. This often precedes violent moves. A spread widening from 0.01% to 0.05% means liquidity has dropped 80%. Don't submit market orders in wide-spread conditions.

setup_name: Multi-Timeframe Exit — HTF Signal Override
keywords: multi-timeframe, MTF, higher timeframe, signal override, exit
description: When the higher timeframe (4h for 1h entries, daily for 4h entries) gives an opposing signal, exit regardless of the lower timeframe. A 1h entry against a 4h trend has a 70%+ failure rate. Always defer to the higher timeframe. The MTF exit is the ultimate filter against being on the wrong side of the big picture.

setup_name: Triple Top/Bottom Exit — Chart Pattern Completion
keywords: triple top, triple bottom, chart pattern, completion, exit
description: When price tests the same level 3 times and fails, exit. Triple tops signal selling pressure. Triple bottoms signal buying support. After the third test fails, reversal probability is 75%+. Exit 100% at the third test failure. In trending markets, triple tops often become continuation flags — use ADX>25 to filter.

setup_name: ATR-Based Profit Target — Dynamic Exit
keywords: ATR, average true range, profit target, dynamic exit, volatility
description: Set profit targets at ATR multiples: 1.5x ATR for scalps, 3x ATR for day trades, 5x ATR for swings. This automatically adapts to volatility. Current BTC 1h ATR is ~1.2%, so targets would be: scalp 1.8%, day trade 3.6%, swing 6%. Compare the ATR target to your entry-stop distance to ensure minimum 2:1 R:R.

setup_name: Opening Range Exit — First 15 Minutes Range
keywords: opening range, first 15 minutes, range, exit, day trading
description: Define the first 15 minutes' range. If price breaks the range and then reverses back, exit immediately. Failed breakouts from this range are high-probability reversal signals. Target the opposite side for the reversal. For crypto, use the London Open (07:00 UTC) or NY Open (13:30 UTC) range.

setup_name: Divergence Exhaustion — Multi-Indicator Convergence
keywords: divergence, exhaustion, multi-indicator, RSI, MACD, volume
description: When 2+ indicators show bearish divergence simultaneously (price higher but RSI lower + MACD lower + volume declining), exit 100%. Single divergences: 50-60% accuracy. Dual divergences: 70-75%. Triple divergences: 80%+. Each additional diverging indicator increases reversal probability by 10-15%.

setup_name: Circuit Breaker Exit — Drawdown Chain
keywords: circuit breaker, drawdown, chain, consecutive losses, pause
description: If you have 3 consecutive losing trades, tighten all stops by 50% and reduce position sizes by 50%. If you have 5 consecutive losses, stop trading for the day. Consecutive losses signal either a regime change or psychological breakdown. Neither is fixable by trading more.

setup_name: Scaling Out at Resistance — Liquidity-Based Exit
keywords: scale out, resistance, liquidity, aggressive sellers, partial exit
description: When approaching resistance with aggressive sellers (volume spike at the offer), scale out 50% immediately. If the level holds, exit the remaining 50%. If it breaks with volume, re-enter with 75% of original size. This is optimal when you can see order flow — exiting into strength.

setup_name: Time-Based Profit Target — Maximum Hold Duration by R
keywords: time based, profit target, maximum hold, R multiple, duration
description: If a trade reaches 0.5R within 25% of its time window, it's on track — hold. If breakeven or negative at 50% of time window, exit. If it hasn't reached 1R by 75%, exit at market. For 48-hour max hold on 1h: 0-12h = develop, 12-24h = must be green, 24-36h = must be at 1R+, 36-48h = exit regardless.

setup_name: Dead Trade Exit — No Progress Signal
keywords: dead trade, no progress, flat, sideways, opportunity cost
description: If a trade is flat (within 0.3% of entry) after 8 bars on 1h, it's a dead trade — exit. Dead trades consume margin, attention, and emotional energy. They have a 55% chance of becoming a loser and only 45% chance of reaching 1R. Exit and deploy capital into a fresh setup. Opportunity cost is a real cost.

setup_name: Bollinger %b Reversal Exit — Overbought/Oversold Exit
keywords: bollinger, %b, overbought, oversold, mean reversion, exit
description: For mean reversion trades, exit when Bollinger %b reaches the opposite extreme. Longs entered at %b < 0.20 should exit when %b > 0.80. Shorts entered at %b > 0.80 should exit when %b < 0.20. This ensures symmetrical entry-exit logic. For trending trades, exit when %b reverses from > 0.85 to < 0.50.

setup_name: ADX Decline Exit — Trend Strength Fading
keywords: ADX, decline, trend strength, fading, exit signal
description: When ADX drops below 25 after being above 35, trend strength is fading. Exit 50% of trending positions. When ADX drops below 20, exit 100% and switch to range parameters. ADX decline from 35 to 25 is a weaker trend. ADX decline from 25 to 20 is a dying trend. Don't hold trending positions in dying trends.

setup_name: Stop Hunt Reversal Exit — False Breakout
keywords: stop hunt, false breakout, liquidity grab, reversal, institutional
description: When price breaks a key level and immediately reverses back (stop hunt), exit and reverse. The institutional playbook: sweep stops below support to accumulate, then push price up. If you see a wick below support followed by a strong close above, that's a stop hunt. Exit shorts immediately and consider going long. This pattern has 70%+ win rate in crypto.

setup_name: Relative Volume Exit — Volume Dry-Up Warning
keywords: relative volume, dry up, warning, exit, volume decline
description: When volume drops below 50% of its 20-period moving average during a trending move, it signals exhaustion. The move lacks fuel. Exit 50% at 0.5x volume. Exit 100% at 0.3x volume. Volume is the fuel of trends — without it, trends die. This exit is especially powerful when combined with RSI divergence.
